qa_pairs.source_title: Achieving Balanced Crystallinity of Donor and Acceptor by Combining Blade-Coating and Ternary Strategies in Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: Explain the error associated with estimating the electron affinity (EA) of organic semiconductors using the optical bandgap and ionization potential.
qa_pairs.answer: Organic semiconductors typically have a large exciton binding energy, often exceeding 0.3 eV. Because of this high binding energy, simply subtracting the optical bandgap from the ionization potential (IP) fails to account for the energy required to separate the exciton into free charges, leading to substantial errors in EA estimation.
qa_pairs.source_title: Electronic Structure Characterization of Soft Semiconductors

qa_pairs.question: Compare the photovoltaic performance metrics of the all-polymer solar cell based on PT8:P(NDI2HD-T) with those of the PTFS8-based device.
qa_pairs.answer: The PT8:P(NDI2HD-T) based device achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 8.00%, an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 1.05 V, a short-circuit current (JSC) of 11.10 mA cm⁻², and a fill factor (FF) of 68.5%. In contrast, the PTFS8-based device exhibits a much lower PCE of 0.63%, primarily due to poor charge transfer caused by a marginal HOMO-HOMO offset with the acceptor.
qa_pairs.source_title: Understanding the impact of side-chains on photovoltaic performance in efficient all-polymer solar cells

qa_pairs.question: Why does the PTF8-based solar cell exhibit a significantly higher open-circuit voltage (VOC) than the PT8-based device?
qa_pairs.answer: The increase in VOC from 1.05 V (PT8) to 1.22 V (PTF8) is a direct result of the lower (deeper) HOMO energy level induced by fluorination, which increases the energy gap between the donor's HOMO and the acceptor's LUMO.
qa_pairs.source_title: Understanding the impact of side-chains on photovoltaic performance in efficient all-polymer solar cells

qa_pairs.question: Compare the power conversion efficiency (PCE) and hole mobility of NMeTTB-based devices to TTB-based devices.
qa_pairs.answer: NMeTTB-based devices exhibit significantly higher performance, achieving a PCE of 1.8% and a hole mobility of approximately 2 x 10^-4 cm^2/(Vs). In contrast, TTB-based devices show a much lower PCE of 0.1% and a hole mobility of only ~10^-7 cm^2/(Vs).
qa_pairs.source_title: Investigation of Phase Separation in Bulk Heterojunction Solar Cells via Supramolecular Chemistry

qa_pairs.question: What are the photovoltaic performance metrics for the top-performing solar cell based on the PTB7-Th:H-di-PDI blend?
qa_pairs.answer: The PTB7-Th:H-di-PDI based device achieved a maximum power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 6.41%, a short-circuit current (Jsc) of 13.12 mA cm⁻², an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 0.79 V, and a fill factor (FF) of 0.60.
qa_pairs.source_title: Influence of Molecular Geometry of Perylene Diimide Dimers and Polymers on Bulk Heterojunction Morphology Toward High-Performance Nonfullerene Polymer Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: What is the peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) value for the PTB7-Th:H-di-PDI device, and at what wavelength is it observed?
qa_pairs.answer: The top-performing PTB7-Th:H-di-PDI device reached a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 70% at a wavelength of 540 nm.
qa_pairs.source_title: Influence of Molecular Geometry of Perylene Diimide Dimers and Polymers on Bulk Heterojunction Morphology Toward High-Performance Nonfullerene Polymer Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: What are the photovoltaic performance metrics of the reference polymer DPP4T in an organic solar cell?
qa_pairs.answer: The reference polymer DPP4T achieved an optimal power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 4.0 ± 0.3%, with a short-circuit current (Jsc) of 9.2 ± 0.3 mA/cm² and an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 0.66 ± 0.02 V.
qa_pairs.source_title: Effects of Alkyl Side Chains Positioning and Presence of Fused Aromatic Units in the Backbone of Low-Bandgap Diketopyrrolopyrrole Copolymers on the Optoelectronic Properties of Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: What are the photovoltaic performance parameters for the champion binary organic solar cell based on the PM1:A-OSeF blend?
qa_pairs.answer: The champion PM1:A-OSeF-based device achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 18.5%, with an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 0.880 V, a short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 27.2 mA/cm², and a fill factor (FF) of 77.3%.
qa_pairs.source_title: Optimized Crystal Framework by Asymmetric Core Isomerization in Selenium-Substituted Acceptor for Efficient Binary Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: Which two factors are intrinsically linked to the maximum achievable efficiency of semitransparent organic solar cells?
qa_pairs.answer: The maximum achievable efficiency is intrinsically linked to the specific shape of the External Quantum Efficiency (EQE) spectrum and the target transparency level of the device.
qa_pairs.source_title: Efficiency Limits and Color of Semitransparent Organic Solar Cells for Application in Building-Integrated Photovoltaics

qa_pairs.question: Why is spectral engineering necessary to reach the thermodynamic limits of semitransparent organic solar cells?
qa_pairs.answer: Spectral engineering is necessary because the maximum efficiency of these cells depends on specific EQE shapes tailored to different transparency values. Optimizing these spectral shapes is essential to maximize performance while maintaining the desired level of light transmission.
qa_pairs.source_title: Efficiency Limits and Color of Semitransparent Organic Solar Cells for Application in Building-Integrated Photovoltaics

qa_pairs.question: What is the effect of adding 0.5 vol% of 1,6-diiodohexane (DIH) on the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of PBTTPD/PC71BM solar cells?
qa_pairs.answer: The addition of 0.5 vol% DIH as a solvent additive increases the PCE of PBTTPD/PC71BM (1:1.5, w/w) solar cells from 5.0% to 7.3%. This represents a relative improvement of 45% in device efficiency.
qa_pairs.source_title: Improving Device Efficiency of Polymer/Fullerene Bulk Heterojunction Solar Cells Through Enhanced Crystallinity and Reduced Grain Boundaries Induced by Solvent Additives

qa_pairs.question: How does the short-circuit current density (JSC) change when DIH is used in the processing of PBTTPD/PC71BM devices?
qa_pairs.answer: The short-circuit current density (JSC) increases significantly from 9 mA/cm² in devices processed without additives to 13.1 mA/cm² in devices processed with DIH. This constitutes a 40% increase in current density.
qa_pairs.source_title: Improving Device Efficiency of Polymer/Fullerene Bulk Heterojunction Solar Cells Through Enhanced Crystallinity and Reduced Grain Boundaries Induced by Solvent Additives

qa_pairs.question: What are the photovoltaic performance parameters of the champion ternary organic solar cell based on the PTzBI-dF:CH1007:BT-4BO blend?
qa_pairs.answer: The champion ternary organic solar cell, utilizing a PTzBI-dF:CH1007:BT-4BO blend at a weight ratio of 1:0.3:0.8, achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 17.80%. This performance is characterized by an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 0.88 V, a short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 26.90 mA/cm², and a fill factor (FF) of 75.35%.
qa_pairs.source_title: Formation of Vitrified Solid Solution Enables Simultaneously Efficient and Stable Organic Solar Cells
